item.content:encoded:
Against the odds, Nolan Arenado is a 30-home run hitter for the Diamondbacks
Arenado joined a short list of third basemen with eight different 30-home run seasons, with the benchmark of 400 for his career within reach next season.
(Photo by Orlando Ramirez/Getty Images)
SAN DIEGO — Nolan Arenado hit 28 home runs combined over the previous two seasons before the Arizona Diamondbacks traded for the third baseman last offseason.
Defense and leadership were the baseline expectations for Arenado in Arizona, and whatever was left in the tank offensively was bonus.
In his age 35 campaign, Arenado has clubbed 30 home runs, punishing a hanging slider from San Diego Padres pitcher Casey Mize on Friday to hit a mark he had not reached since 2022. That year, Arenado was a finalist for the National League MVP with the St. Louis Cardinals.
He has experienced some quieter times since then, suggesting he declined to the point where he could no longer be relied on as an impact bat for a lineup.
The potential future Hall of Famer has reversed time this season for a team that has sorely needed the production.
“It meant a lot,” Arenado told Arizona Sports after hitting his 30th home run. “Just from where I started and just where I’ve been the last couple of years. It hasn’t been easy, but I just thank God that I’ve been healthy. And I owe a lot of credit to the hitting coaches for challenging me and all these guys for challenging me to take chances and work on things.”
Nolan Arenado is on a HEATER!
9 HR in September, 30 HR on the season 😯 pic.twitter.com/1ZcIDpDnmo
— MLB (@MLB) September 26, 2026
Arenado was visibly amped running the bases after the blast that put the D-backs ahead 6-2 in a must-win game they would take 11-4. The Southern California native also did it in front of his parents and brother, who made the hour drive south to watch him play.
“That was really cool,” Arenado said.
This is the eighth time Arenado has hit 30 home runs in a season. 28 players all-time have more such seasons and only two while spending most of their time at third base, per Stathead: Hall of Famers Mike Schmidt (12) and Eddie Mathews (10).
Arenado did so from 2015-19 and picked the streak back up after the shortened 2020 campaign in 2021-22.
This is the outlier outside his prime, especially after he hit 12 home runs last season.
“He has regained a lot of that offensive magic that’s been with him for so long,” manager Torey Lovullo said.
When asked about his offense’s recent success, Diamondbacks general manager Mike Hazen said on Friday, “We’re hitting more home runs. Arenado’s hitting a home run every night.”
Arenado has homered nine times in September, second in Major League Baseball to Baltimore’s Pete Alonso (11). He owns an .889 OPS in the second half of this season. And his four home runs in the past five games have come at a time when the Diamondbacks have had to win to keep their playoff hopes alive.
Arenado joked on the Diamondbacks TV broadcast Friday night that he is probably making Arizona’s hitting coaches work harder than they ever had before. He gave hitting coach Joe Mather a big hug in the dugout after going yard.
Arenado came to Arizona with a reputation of being a maniacal competitor and worker.
He has aimed to challenge himself during his preparation before games to get his body up to speed at this age, not totally dissimilar to Eugenio Suarez when he turned around his 2024 season in Arizona. The veteran has said lately he has cooled off the pregame physical work to maintain his body this late in the season, which has paid off.
Health has also been a factor, as Arenado dealt with shoulder issues at the end of his St. Louis tenure that he felt hampered him. He has been banged up in the second half of this season (intercostal, thumb) but has managed to limit his time off the field.
Before Friday’s game, Arenado stood in the batter’s box with his headphones and a bat, practicing his load and stride. Nobody was throwing batting practice yet, and there were still tamps and other grounds-keeping equipment on the field. Perhaps he was visualizing what soon became reality when he shot a ball into the Western Metal Supply Co. building.
Lars Nootbaar has had a front-row seat to Arenado’s career since he came up with the Cardinals in 2021, reuniting with the veteran at this past trade deadline.
“I just think that if anybody saw what he does and what he goes through on a daily basis and to try to get himself in a good position and be as obsessive as he is and be as passionate as he is, to get rewarded in this game and to be able to hit 30 in front of his family, that’s really cool from a baseball fan perspective and friend,” Nootbaar said.
Geraldo Perdomo predicted this re-breakout season back in spring training, and he claims to have called Arenado going for 30 home runs a couple weeks ago.
“I’m happy for him,” Perdomo said. “He’s the type of player who works every day hard in the cages with the hitting coaches to get better.”
Arenado enters Saturday second among qualified D-backs hitters with an .803 OPS, ahead of Corbin Carroll and Ketel Marte and trailing Gabriel Moreno.
He has previously been candid about wishing he has had more success this year with runners in scoring position, a shortcoming for large chunks of the season both individually and team-wide. He is batting .228 in those spots, although the OPS has climbed to .745.
This is not quite the MVP-candidate version of Arenado’s prime, but there is no doubt that the Diamondbacks acquiring him from St. Louis without having to pay the majority of his contract was a steal. It is arguably the biggest win of Hazen’s offseason.
Arenado is up to 383 career home runs, as the celebrated 400 benchmark is within grasp in 2027. MLB also revealed the 20 top-selling jerseys for the 2026 season, and Arenado was 19th on the list, the highest Diamondback.
For now and most importantly, with the D-backs trailing the final NL Wild Card spot by one game with two to play, can Arenado push this hot streak a couple games further?

item.content:encoded:
SAN DIEGO (AP) — Nolan Arenado hit one of Arizona's three home runs and Geraldo Perdomo drove in four runs for the Diamondbacks, who beat San Diego 11-4 on Friday night to remain alive for the National League's final wild-card spot.
Lars Nootbar and Jordan Lawlar also homered in the victory, which kept San Diego from clinching the No. 4 seed and home-field advantage in the wild-card round next week.
Brandon Pfaadt (8-3) beat the Padres for the third time this season with 7 2/3 innings. He allowed four runs and nine hits, struck out seven and walked two.
San Diego and Chicago clinched wild-card berths on Thursday, leaving Philadelphia and Arizona to fight it out for the third spot. Arizona is one game behind the Phillies with two to play.
The Diamondbacks and Padres knew that the Cubs had been swept by Boston in a doubleheader and that Philadelphia had lost to Tampa Bay.
The Padres then just needed to beat the Diamondbacks to clinch the No. 4 seed.
But Casey Mize (6-10) allowed the three home runs to jeopardize his spot on the wild-card roster and the Padres were booed a few times a night after clinching their club-record third straight postseason berth with a 4-2 win at the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Nootbar drove Mize's first pitch into the home-run porch in the right-field corner. Perdomo hit an RBI triple and Corbin Carroll a sacrifice fly to make it 3-0.
Lawlar homered to right field with one out in the second. Arenado drove a two-run shot off the third level of the Western Metal Supply Co. brick warehouse in the left-field corner with two outs in the third, his 30th, for a 6-2 lead.
Gabriel Moreno hit an RBI single in the fourth and, after Kyle Hart walked the bases loaded in the sixth, Perdomo cleared them with a double that bounced off the glove of retreating center fielder Jackson Merrill and then off the padded fence.
Padres center fielder Jase Bowen robbed Perdomo of a home run to end the eighth and then stole one from Tim Tawa to end the ninth.
Up next
Arizona was pondering its options for Saturday night after placing RHP Corbin Burnes on the injured list with shoulder inflammation. The Padres will go with RHP Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.56 ERA).

item.content:encoded:
What began as a blowout deficit ended in a close loss as the Colorado Rockies’ last chance at some “LoDo Magic” fell short in a 12-8 loss to the Arizona Diamondbacks. The Rockies suffered the sweep while finishing 32-49 at Coors Field this season.
Attack of the Snakes
The first inning has been a disaster for the Rockies most of the season, but especially during their slide over the last few weeks. There was hope with Tanner Gordon on the mound, who has had strong numbers in the first inning and could buck the trend and start the team off with a solid chance in the final home game.
The Diamondbacks had other intentions.
Lars Nootbar started the game with a hot shot down the first-base line that TJ Rumfield managed to stop from going for extra bases. However, Gordon was late getting off the mound and it turned into an infield single. Gordon then walked Ketel Marte, followed by a three-run home run off the bat of Gabriel Moreno to make it 3-0.
Geraldo Perdomo then launched a ball to center field for a triple before coming in to score on a bloop single to left field by Pavin Smith for the fourth run of the inning. Nolan Arenado then followed with his 29th home run of the season, a two-run shot to make it 6-0.
Gordon finally escaped the inning, but six runs in the first brought the total number of runs allowed in the opening frame of the series to 13. The Rockies have also allowed a run in the first in 12 of their last 17 games.
The Diamondbacks kept the foot on the gas in the second inning as Nootbar singled to lead off and scored on Marte’s RBI double. Perdomo later blooped a single into shallow center field to score another run, making it 8-0 after two innings.
After a scoreless third inning, Gordon’s day would come to an end early in the fourth inning. Perdomo led off the inning with a walk, the fourth of the game and a new career high for Gordon. Smith’s then delivered an RBI double. Gordon managed to strike out Arenado, but then surrendered a single to Corbin Carroll to end his afternoon, but was still tagged for the 10th Arizona run when James McCann singled to left field off reliever Jimmy Herget.
Gordon lasted just 3.1 innings, allowing 10 runs on 12 hits with four walks and just one strikeout. The Diamondbacks were not fooled by his fastball, meaning he had to rely on his secondary pitches, which he struggled to command. When he did have to throw a fastball, Arizona made sure to square up the ball and do damage. Despite pounding the zone as usual, Gordon threw 96 pitches and induced three groundouts and five flyouts, but only had three swings and misses.
The Bullpen Fire Brigade
Having to take on another heavy workload, the bullpen did an admirable job settling down the Diamondbacks offense.
Herget picked up 2.2 innings of work and was solid enough despite giving up an RBI single to Arenado in the fifth inning and a McCann home run in the sixth inning to make it 12-1. He still managed four strikeouts against one walk while surrendering four hits, but his 49 pitches helped navigate to the later frames.
Nick Frasso and Juan Mejia then followed with scoreless seventh and eighth innings, respectively, setting the tone after the Diamondbacks had started subbing out players. Jordan Romano then took over the ninth and, despite giving up a triple, fired a clean inning.
E-Rod Domination
While the Diamondback offense had a productive day at the plate against Gordon, the Rockies offense couldn’t quite figure out Eduardo Rodriguez. The veteran left-hander breezed his way through six innings, allowing just two runs on nine hits with three strikeouts. Utilizing four grounders and seven easy flyouts, Rodriguez threw 92 pitches and stayed in the zone consistently. He had a 63% first-pitch strike rate and 12 swings and misses. His changeup was particularly effective, generating a 21% whiff rate.
The Rockies scratched across their first run in the fourth inning against Rodriguez when Rumfield singled to lead off. Cole Carrigg and Kyle Karros both singled to then load the bases. Brett Sullivan then hit into a fielder’s choice that allowed the run to score, but put runners on the corners with one out. Unfortunately, the Rockies couldn’t scratch across any other runs. The next run wouldn’t come across until the sixth inning when Karros sent a belt-high fastball into left field for his 13th home run of the season, making it 12-2 Diamondbacks.
Here Come the Rockies!
Once Rodriguez was out of the game, the Rockies had begun a line change of their own in the seventh inning, but started to find some success against the Arizona bullpen.
Facing Dennis Santana, Zac Veen led off with a double down the line. Two batters later, Hunter Goodman delivered a one-out RBI single after a lengthy at-bat to make it 12-3.
Rumfield followed with a walk, setting the table for Carrigg to hit a three-run home run. It was his 11th of the season and got the Rockies back within six runs.
Taylor Clarke then took over the Diamondbacks in the eighth inning and ran into more trouble from the Rockies offense. Veen kicked off another rally with a towering home run to right field for his third of the season to make it 12-7.
Adael Amador then barrelled up a baseball to right for a double. After Goodman recorded the second out on a line drive, Rumfield lined a double to right to drive in another run and make it 12-8. With that double, Rumfield also tied Troy Tulowitzki for most times reaching safely in a rookie season at 243. Karros then threatened with a long fly ball that was caught shortly before the wall in left field to end the inning.
Unfortunately, the rally magic ran out as Kevin Ginkel worked a clean ninth inning to put the Rockies away. In the game, the Rockies had 17 hits, while striking out eight times against one walk. Carrigg led the way with four hits while four other hitters had two hits. They went 5-for-13 with runners in scoring position but left 10 on base.
Meanwhile, Arizona had 18 hits with seven strikeouts and five walks while going 6-for-15 with RISP. Oddly enough, they also left 10 men on base, but had three batters with three hits.
Up Next
The Rockies head off to the South Side of Chicago to take on the White Sox for the final three-game series of the season. Tomoyuki Sugano (菅野 智之) will face off against Sean Burke.
First pitch is at 5:40 pm MDT.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

23 Sep 2026, 12:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Brad Penner)
Drew Rasmussen allowed one hit in 6 2/3 outstanding innings and the visiting Tampa Bay Rays clinched the American League East with a 6-1 victory over the New York Yankees on Tuesday night in the nightcap of a day-night doubleheader.
The Rays won for the 20th time in 28 games and clinched their fifth division title. Tampa Bay last won the AL East in 2021 when it won a team-record 100 games. Yandy Diaz drove in four runs on a pair of singles.
Rasmussen (16-5) took a no-hitter into the seventh until Heliot Ramos opened the inning with a double to left for New York. Ramos eventually scored on an RBI single by rookie George Lombard Jr. off Kevin Kelly.
Rasmussen finished with 11 strikeouts for his fourth career double-digit strikeout performance. He finished two shy of his career-high set June 10 against the Boston Red Sox and the Rays won his 12th consecutive start.
Yankees 2, Rays 0 (Game 1)
Cody Bellinger hit a two-run home run in the fourth inning as host New York recorded a shutout over Tampa Bay in the opener of a day-night doubleheader.
With the victory, the Yankees temporarily prevented the Rays from clinching the AL East and moved six games ahead of the Boston Red Sox for the American League's top wild-card spot.
New York's Carlos Rodon (7-3) scattered three singles over eight innings as the Yankees finished off the victory in a brisk 2 hours, 2 minutes. Rodon struck out eight in his 100th career win and also reached 1,500 strikeouts for his career. Rays right-hander Nick Martinez (15-5) allowed two runs on five hits over six innings with seven strikeouts to take his first loss since July 9.
Dodgers 7, Padres 0
Freddie Freeman drove in three runs, Will Smith and Tommy Edman hit home runs, and Los Angeles inched closer to the best record in the National League with a shutout of visiting San Diego.
Eight Dodgers pitchers held down the red-hot Padres offense in a bullpen game, with Justin Wrobleski (12-5) earning the win. Roki Sasaki struck out two in one inning in his return from a blister issue. The Dodgers extended their home winning streak to 11 games.
Los Angeles moved to within one game of the NL-best Milwaukee Brewers and reduced its magic number for a top-two NL spot and a bye into the National League Division Series to one. Luis Campusano had two hits for the Padres, whose magic number to clinch a playoff spot remained at two.
Phillies 6, Brewers 4
Bryson Stott delivered the tiebreaking hit in the eighth inning to guide Philadelphia to a victory over visiting Milwaukee. Brandon Marsh homered and knocked in three runs as the Phillies lowered their magic number to two to clinch a postseason berth.
Zack Wheeler ended up with a no-decision after striking out 11 while giving up three runs and five hits in 5 2/3 innings. Wheeler struck out the first seven batters he faced, setting a Phillies record for consecutive strikeouts to begin a game. His first-inning strikeout of Brice Turang was the 2,000th of his career.
The Brewers saw their lead over the Dodgers for the top record in the majors shrink to one as they lost just the third time in their last 13 games. William Contreras knocked in three runs.
Marlins 8, Cubs 2 (12 innings)
Griffin Conine plated the go-ahead run that ignited a six-run 12th inning for visiting Miami, which snapped a three-game losing by beating Chicago and postponing the Cubs' playoff celebration for at least a day.
On a night when runs were scarce until the final inning, both teams endured a pair of scoreless extra frames before Conine broke the drought with a leadoff, golf-shot single off Caleb Thielbar that fell just inside the left field line. Esteury Ruiz, the automatic runner, scored from second to make it 3-2 as the Marlins sent 10 batters to the plate in the inning.
The Cubs could have clinched a wild-card playoff spot with a win or Arizona loss, but neither of those happened keeping the Diamondbacks mathematically alive. Josh Ekness (3-4) struck out a pair in the 11th inning to get the win while Thielbar (3-4) gave up three runs -- two earned -- in his inning of work.
Guardians 3, Red Sox 2
Nathaniel Lowe drove in Chase DeLauter with a sacrifice fly in the ninth inning and Cleveland held on to beat host Boston in the first game of a three-game series.
Cleveland not only extended its winning streak to six but maintained its one-game lead over the Chicago White Sox for first place in the AL Central.
Parker Messick held Boston to one run on five hits in five innings, his 14th straight start allowing three runs or fewer. Payton Tolle started for the Red Sox and gave up two runs on eight hits in 5 2/3 innings as the Guardians went 1-for-12 with runners in scoring position and stranded 15.
White Sox 14, Royals 11
Chase Meidroth smacked a three-run home run among his three hits and drove in five, and Brenton Doyle, Randal Grichuk and Munetaka Murakami also homered to power Chicago past host Kansas City.
Chicago won for the fourth time in five games to remain one game behind the AL Central-leading Cleveland Guardians. The White Sox, who hold the third and final AL wild-card spot, reduced their magic number to earn a playoff berth to three.
Vinnie Pasquantino hit a ninth-inning grand slam for the Royals, who lost their fifth straight. He went 3-for-5 with a double and also drove in five.
Nationals 3, Tigers 1
CJ Abrams hit a pair of home runs and drove in all three runs as visiting Washington topped Detroit. Abrams reached 100 RBIs for the season with his solo shot in the second inning, then broke a 1-1 tie in the seventh with his 33rd long ball of the season, a two-run blast.
Dylan Crews had two hits and scored the other run for the Nationals. Rookie Jackson Kent (2-4) earned the win in long relief. He allowed one run on six hits over four innings and struck out three. Opener Riley Cornelio lasted 2 2/3 innings, striking out four and walking three.
Ben Malgeri scored the Tigers' only run. Kevin McGonigle and Max Clark each had two hits.
Pirates 2, Cardinals 0
Jared Jones and two relievers combined on a one-hitter as Pittsburgh beat visiting St. Louis for a fifth straight win. Jones (5-6) lowered his ERA to 1.08 in four September starts and struck out nine with zero walks over seven innings while throwing 63 of his 86 pitches for strikes.
Pittsburgh broke a scoreless tie with two outs in the sixth inning on Ryan O'Hearn's RBI single against Andre Pallante (12-8). Pallante allowed one run on three hits with two walks and two strikeouts over six innings.
St. Louis struck out 14 times and lost for the fifth time in its last six games.
Astros 7, Mariners 0
Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as Houston slugged and pitched its way past host Seattle.
Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros, who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the West. Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings of relief.
Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle. The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine.
Reds 4, Braves 0
Brandon Williamson fired six scoreless innings and Cincinnati supported him with three solo homers to defeat host Atlanta in the opener of a three-game series.
Cincinnati ended a two-game losing streak and evened the season series with Atlanta at 2-2. Williamson (5-4) worked six scoreless innings, allowing three hits and two strikeouts. Elly De La Cruz (29), Dane Myers (8) and Eugenio Suarez (25) each hit a home run for the Reds. It was Suarez's 350th career homer, making him the 10th active player to reach that mark.
Atlanta starter JR Ritchie (1-4) pitched five innings and allowed one run on four hits and three walks. The rookie struck out a career-high eight batters.
Mets 6, Rangers 3
Francisco Alvarez laced a go-ahead two-run double in the sixth, then scored an insurance run on an unusual sacrifice fly for visiting New York, who damaged Texas' playoff hopes with a win in the opener of a three-game interleague series in Arlington.
Juan Soto had an RBI single in the third, and Carson Benge capped the scoring with a run-scoring double in the seventh for the Mets. The club won hours after removing the interim tag from manager Andy Green and signing him to a three-year extension.
Josh Jung had an RBI double in the third, and Elias Diaz and Wyatt Langford lofted sacrifice flies in the fourth for the Rangers, who entered Tuesday with a one-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West.
Diamondbacks 7, Rockies 2
Nolan Arenado homered and doubled among his three hits, Michael Soroka tossed seven strong innings, and Arizona kept its slim postseason hopes alive with a win over host Colorado in Denver.
Geraldo Perdomo also had three hits and Ildemaro Vargas finished with two hits for Arizona, which remains alive in the NL wild-card race, sitting four games behind Philadelphia, San Diego and the Chicago Cubs for the third and final spot with five games to go.
Mickey Moniak homered for Colorado, which finished with just three hits and just one after the third inning. The Rockies (57-100) are the first team to lose 100 or more games in four straight seasons since the 1962-65 New York Mets.
Twins 3, Giants 2
Walker Jenkins homered, Luke Keaschall contributed both offensively and defensively, and Minnesota evened its road interleague series against San Francisco.
Taj Bradley (12-6) combined with four relievers on a six-hitter for the Twins, who used two late diving catches by Keaschall in right field to prevent the Giants from taking the first two of the series.
Bradley allowed just one other hit -- a fifth-inning single by Drew Gilbert -- in his six innings. He walked three and struck out six. Keaschall's one-out triple scored Ryan Kreidler, then Brooks Lee gave Minnesota the lead for good with a run-scoring single to plate Keaschall.
A's 9, Angels 7
Carlos Cortes hit a go-ahead two-run homer in the bottom of the eighth inning and the Athletics overcame a six-run deficit to beat Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif.
In addition to the homer off Sam Bachman, Cortes also delivered a pinch-hit RBI triple in the seventh, helping the Athletics end a six-game losing streak. Zack Gelof hit a two-run homer later in the eighth for the A's. Shea Langeliers and Lawrence Butler each had three hits and an RBI for the Athletics.
Denzer Guzman homered and drove in four RBIs for the Angels, who have lost four of their last six games. Mike Trout added three hits and two runs for Los Angeles (60-97), which has never lost 100 games in a season.
Blue Jays at Orioles, ppd.
The scheduled game between Toronto and host Baltimore was postponed due to ongoing inclement weather. The game will be made up as part of a split doubleheader on Wednesday, with games starting at 1:35 p.m. and 6:35 p.m. ET.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
It wasn’t the (potential) final Coors Field game Kyle Freeland dreamed of.
Unfortunately, the Rockies lost their 100th game of the season, and he only pitched three innings in the loss. The Rockies mustered just eight baserunners, and only two came around to score early in the game they lost to the Arizona Diamondbacks, 7-2.
(Potential) Coors Field Swan Song
In what could be Kyle Freeland’s final start at Coors Field as a Rockie, he wasn’t very sharp. He gave up a lead-off single to Ildemaro Vargas, but then got Rockies-killer Ketel Marte to pop out to short. Following that, Gabriel Moreno doubled to score Vargas, and Geraldo Perdomo singled to score Moreno and put the Diamondbacks up 2-0. Nolan Arenado singled to reach base for the 11th time in 11 games against the Rockies this year, but then Freeland was able to strike out Jordan Lawlar. Other Rockies-killer Corbin Carroll added another run on another double before Tim Tawa walked to load the bases. However, Jose Fernandez grounded out to end the inning.
Freeland allowed just a single to Marte in the second, but then gave up a lead-off double to Arenado in the third. Lawlar grounded out and Carroll lined out, but then Tawa hit a ground-rule double — the fourth of the ballgame — to score Arenado. Fernandez struck out on a foul tip to end the inning.
Freeland came out for the fourth, but allowed a single to Vargas that turned into two bases when Zac Veen committed an error. Unfortunately, that was the end for the Denver native in this game. His final line: 3.0 IP, 9 H, 5 ER, 1 BB, 2 K. He threw 69 pitches, 44 for strikes.
“I think he was behind in counts early,” manager Warren Schaeffer said, noting that the Diamondbacks had “a good plan.”
“I don’t think he was as sharp in the zone,” he added.
When his press conference had ended, Schaeffer added this: “This guy’s meant to much to our organization over the years, and the ultimate pro. You hate to see it end like that.” Schaeffer thanked him for his contributions on the field and in the community.
“Not how you want to draw it up,” an emotional Freeland said, thanking his teammates, coaches, family, and fans.
“It was an emotional day,” he noted. “I made sure to soak up every single minute of it.”
Freeland added to fans, “I appreciate you so much. I love you so much,” adding, “I’m proud to be a Colorado Rockie.”
Baserunners galore, but runs no more
The Rockies offense was befuddled by Michael Soroka early, but finally broke through in the third inning. Mickey Moniak broke out of his slump with a solo shot to right-center to break up the shutout.
Troy Johnston then doubled and Veen reached on an error by Tawa. Jake McCarthy grounded into a force out that nabbed Veen at second, and then Johnston came around to score on a Connor Norby sac fly, cutting the lead in half, 4-2.
Unfortunately, McCarthy tried to do McCarthy things and was picked off trying to steal second. And even more unfortunately, the next eight were retired until Norby walked with two outs in the sixth. But then TJ Rumfield flied out to left to end the threat.
In the seventh, Cole Carrigg was hit by a pitch after Hunter Goodman struck out, and then Kyle Karros and Moniak struck out. In the eighth, Johnston was hit by a 99.5-mph fastball to kick things off. Veen then flew out to left and McCarthy struck out swinging, snapping his career-best 22-game on-base streak. Norby struck out to end the inning and strand another baserunner.
In the ninth, Rumfield flew out to end his 24-game on-base streak — the longest active streak in the Majors and longest by a Rockie since Tyler Freeman’s 25-gamer from June 13-July 12, 2025 — while Goodman grounded out. Carrigg singled for just the third hit of the game, but Karros grounded into a fielder’s choice to end the game.
The Rockies offense mustered eight baserunners all game: three hits, two errors, two hit batters and one walk. The two runs came around to score on the back-to-back hits in the third inning.
Still, Schaeffer remains positive.
“I see a lot of hope, and I see a lot of progress,” he said. “This is obviously not where we want to be.”
He added, “You have to focus on the positives moving forward.”
Gritty Bullpen
Zach Agnos came in to relieve Freeland, immediately getting Marte to ground back out to him. But Moreno hit a sac fly to add another run, 5-2, and then Perdomo singled and stole second. Arenado was called out on strikes to end the inning.
In the fifth, Lawlar led off with a double and Carroll grounded out to Goodman. And Tawa hit a sac fly to score Lawlar from third to make the score 6-2. Fernandez popped out to third to end the inning.
In the sixth, Agnos issued a lead-off walk to Vargas. Luckily, he got the next three batters out. But then Arenado smacked a 421-foot homer to lead off the seventh, putting him a triple away from the cycle (which he would ultimately not get).
Luckily, though, he retired the next three batters thanks in part to a diving play from Carrigg to nab Tawa.
Nick Frasso came in to relieve Agnos in the eighth and was able to pitch a 1-2-3 inning. Juan Mejia took the ninth, and pitched (kind of) a 1-2-3 inning. Moreno grounded out to first and Perdomo singled. Arenado popped out to dash his cycle hopes, and then Perdomo got caught in a rundown trying to steal second to end the inning.
Up Next
The Rockies will look to regroup tomorrow, and the Diamondbacks will look to keep their postseason aspirations alive.
Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09 ERA) will face off against Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA). First pitch is at 6:40pm.
See you then!

item.content:encoded:
DENVER (AP) — Nolan Arenado had his team-leading 28th homer of the season among his three hits, Michael Soroka struck out nine in seven innings of one-run ball and the Arizona Diamondbacks beat Colorado 7-2 Tuesday night, sending the Rockies to their 100th loss of the season.
The victory kept the Diamondbacks four games behind Philadelphia in the race for the third and final NL wild-card spot with five regular-season games remaining for both teams.
The Rockies’ loss made Colorado the first franchise to lose at least 100 games in four consecutive seasons since the New York Mets from 1962-65.
Arenado, a four-time All-Star in his time with Colorado, extended his on-base streak to 16 games. During that stretch, he is batting .379 with seven homers and 14 RBIs.
Gabriel Moreno drove in two runs, giving him 10 RBIs in Arizona’s past 16 games. Geraldo Perdomo added three hits and an RBI for the Diamondbacks.
In four starts against the Rockies this season, Soroka (9-5) has allowed just four earned runs in 23 innings, with 23 strikeouts and six walks.
Kyle Freeland (4-11) took the loss for Colorado, allowing five earned runs in three innings. The Denver native made his final home start of the season for Colorado, where he has played his entire 10-year MLB career.
Mickey Moniak and Connor Norby drove in Colorado’s runs. Moniak hit his 23rd home run of the season. TJ Rumfield and Jake McCarthy failed to record a hit or walk. The two entered the game with the longest active on-base streaks in the majors, with Rumfield at 24 games and McCarthy at 22.
Up next
Arizona RHP Merrill Kelly (9-14, 5.00 ERA) will take on Colorado RHP Mason Adams (0-1, 5.09) on Wednesday in the second game of a three-game series.

Los Arizona Diamondbacks volvieron a demostrar que saben reaccionar cuando están contra las cuerdas. Este domingo, una noche inspirada de Nolan Arenado, quien conectó su tercer grand slam de la temporada, fue clave para que Arizona remontara y derrotara 8-4 a los New York Yankees.
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡José Ramírez llega a las 1,000 carreras impulsadas!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: ¡Los Atlanta Braves aseguran su boleto a los playoffs!
- LEER MÁS SOBRE: New York Yankees 9- 2 Diamondbacks: Resultados y crónica
La jugada que terminó por cambiar el rumbo del encuentro llegó en la quinta entrada. Los Diamondbacks habían conseguido llenar las bases frente al abridor de Nueva York, Will Warren, quien dejó el montículo para darle paso al relevista Brent Headrick.
El pitcher logró retirar a Geraldo Perdomo con un ponche para conseguir el segundo out, pero después vino el descontrol. Headrick otorgó una base por bolas a Corbin Carroll, situación que permitió que Arizona sumara una carrera y dejara las bases listas para Arenado.
Con cuenta de 2-1, el tercera base no perdonó. Arenado encontró el lanzamiento y mandó la pelota por encima de la barda para completar el grand slam y darle la vuelta al partido. Fue el noveno cuadrangular con las bases llenas de su carrera, además de que alcanzó al cubano Yordan Álvarez, de los Houston Astros, como líder de las Grandes Ligas en grand slams durante esta temporada.
Pero el poder ofensivo de Arizona no se limitó a Arenado. Perdomo también tuvo una tarde productiva al conectar un sencillo productor en la primera entrada y posteriormente un triple que llevó otra carrera al plato durante el séptimo episodio.
Los Yankees, por su parte, habían respondido con fuerza en el tercer inning. Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones conectaron cuadrangulares consecutivos dentro de esa entrada frente al abridor de Arizona, Corbin Burnes, para mantener con vida a Nueva York.
Sin embargo, la ofensiva neoyorquina se apagó después de ese episodio. El bullpen de Arizona tomó el control y, encabezado por Justin Martínez, consiguió limitar a los Yankees a solamente tres imparables durante las últimas 6 entradas. Martínez se apuntó la victoria, la tercera de su temporada, con marca de 3-0.

Arenado héroe de Arizona
Con este triunfo, los Diamondbacks llegaron a 47 victorias conseguidas después de comenzar perdiendo, la cifra más alta de las Grandes Ligas. Arizona continúa además en la pelea con los Philadelphia Phillies por el último boleto de comodín de la Liga Nacional, aunque todavía se encuentra cuatro juegos por detrás cuando restan seis encuentros.
Del otro lado, los Yankees aún conservan posibilidades matemáticas de pelear por el Este de la Liga Americana, aunque necesitan cerrar la temporada con victorias y esperar resultados favorables. Nueva York comenzará el martes una serie de cuatro partidos ante los Tampa Bay Rays, actuales líderes divisionales, en territorio neoyorquino.
Por ahora, Arizona celebra una remontada más en una temporada en la que ha convertido los partidos complicados en una de sus principales características. Y esta vez, el golpe decisivo tuvo nombre y apellido: Nolan Arenado.

item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX — The Yankees' chances of winning the AL East title were reduced to nearly zero on Sunday . . . not that they were all that good to begin with.
The Tampa Bay Rays entered Sunday with a magic number of four to eliminate the Yankees from contention for first place. That became three when the Rays beat the Red Sox, and it dropped to two when the Yankees lost to the Arizona Diamondbacks, 8-4.
The Rays (95-60) lead the Yankees (89-66) by six games with seven to play. The two teams will play four games in the Bronx this week, including a split doubleheader on Tuesday. If the Rays win that first game — or any game in the series — the race is over. The Yankees must win all four games to stay alive, and a sweep also would give them the tiebreaker in the season series, 7-6.
The Yankees are scheduled to start lefthanders Carlos Rodon (6-3, 2.95 ERA) and Max Fried (5-4, 2.63) on Tuesday against the Rays, who will counter with righthanders Nick Martinez (15-4, 2.94) and Drew Rasmussen (15-5, 2.72). Gerrit Cole and Cam Schlittler are slated to pitch Wednesday and Thursday for the Yankees.
The Yankees did reduce their magic number to clinch the first wild card — and home-field advantage in the Wild Card Round — to one over the Red Sox, whom they seem likely to play in that round for the second straight season.
The Yankees managed only three hits in the final 6 1/3 innings after hitting three no-doubt home runs off Corbin Burnes in the third inning — 388 feet to left by Heliot Ramos (107.6-mph exit velocity), 424 to left by George Lombard Jr. (108.7) and 448 to center by Spencer Jones (109.8) — for a 4-1 lead, but Arizona's Nolan Arenado capped a five-run fifth with a two-out grand slam off Brent Headrick.
Yankees starter Will Warren retired Tim Tawa to begin the fifth, but Lars Nootbaar doubled, Ketel Marte singled and Gabriel Moreno walked to load the bases. Headrick replaced Warren and struck out Geraldo Perdomo for the second out, but he walked Corbin Carroll to force in a run. One pitch after Arenado's bid for a grand slam went just foul, he gave the Diamondbacks a 6-4 lead with a blast to leftfield.
Perdomo had a run-scoring single in the first and an RBI triple in the seventh as Arizona recorded its MLB-best 47th comeback victory of the season.

item.content:encoded:
The final road game of the 2026 regular season is upon us, as the Yankees will conclude it with a seven-game homestand before likely hosting the Red Sox for the Wild Card Series. If the season ends there, this is the end of the line for the gray uniforms for 2026, but obviously, we all hope we’ll see them next in Tampa (and more) in early October.
Looking to end a road slate that has been very generous to the Yankees on a high note is Will Warren, who’s finishing his sophomore season strong after his great start to the campaign unraveled into a bit of a mess over the summer. Rotation reinforcements that threatened to throw him in the bullpen never came with the recurring injuries, so he’ll finish 2026 with 30 starts for the second straight season. This is No. 29, as he enters with a 3.89 ERA (108 ERA+) and 4.07 FIP in 148 innings. No matter what happens from here, Warren has had a successful year in solidifying himself as a true MLB-caliber rotation arm.
Opposing him will be a former Cy Young winner trying to round into form off Tommy John surgery in Corbin Burnes, whom Yankees fans remember well from his lone season in Baltimore in 2024. Returning from a 16-month absence on September 8 to help with the playoff push, Burnes has allowed five runs across 7.2 innings with six strikeouts to two walks against the Royals and Marlins. He isn’t totally built up, having thrown 75 pitches in his last start, so expect him to settle around 80-85 today. He’s always befuddled the Yankees, pitching to a 1.93 ERA across 23.1 innings in his career, but he doesn’t have a win in any of those four starts.
Ben Rice will once again lead off, followed by Cody Bellinger, Heliot Ramos, and Luis García Jr. We’ve seen better ABs and swings from George Lombard Jr. lately, who’ll bat fifth. Spencer Jones is back after a one-day absence due to a sore foot and will bat in front of Anthony Volpe, Austin Wells, and José Caballero.
Lars Nootbaar will also be a repeat leadoff hitter for the D-backs, followed by Ketel Marte, Gabriel Moreno, and Geraldo Perdomo. Corbin Carroll is batting fifth, Nolan Arenado will bat sixth, and former Blue Jay Jesús Sánchez bats seventh ahead of last night’s hero Pavin Smith and Tim Tawa.
